difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.2.4 at source lines 335-339: a natural transformation gamma : F -> G is an isomorphism in the functor precategory B^A if and only if every component gamma_a is an isomorphism in B. The author's proof (source lines 340-349) treats the two directions by different means. The forward direction is immediate because composition in B^A is componentwise (lines 341-343). The converse is a construction: one must define a candidate natural transformation delta with the given componentwise inverses (lines 345-346) and then verify its naturality axiom by an explicit chain in which the naturality of gamma and the two componentwise inverse identities are consumed in a specific order (line 347), before concluding the two inverse identities from the fact that composition and identities of natural transformations are determined on components (line 348). The statement records only the equivalence of the two notions of isomorphism.
